transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. How are you today? Can you tell me what’s brought you in for our visit?

To be honest, I'm really struggling to cope after a traumatic event that happened about a year and eight months ago. I just feel completely unable to move past it, and it's starting to take over my life. I knew I finally needed to come in and get some help.
Can you tell me if your symptoms started within one month of the event and have lasted less than a month, or if they developed later and have persisted longer?
They definitely didn't just last for a month. They started pretty soon after the event and have persisted the entire time, so I've been dealing with this for about a year and eight months now.
Have you been experiencing flashbacks, nightmares, or intrusive memories about the traumatic event?

Yes, I'm dealing with all of those. During the day, sudden and unwanted memories of the event just pop into my head, and at night, I constantly wake up from vivid nightmares about it. Sometimes, I even lose touch with my surroundings and feel like I'm actually back there reliving it.

{
  "category": "differential point",
  "subcategory": "avoidance and hyperarousal",
  "question": "Have you been avoiding reminders of the trauma, such as people, places, or conversations, and do you feel constantly on edge or easily startled?"

Yes, I absolutely do; I go out of my way to avoid certain people, places, and even conversations that might remind me of what happened. I also feel constantly on edge and incredibly tense, like I can never truly relax even when I'm in a completely safe environment.
